title: Embeddings routing & hosting criteria - discovery call with LucentCommerce
next_steps: Jordan to send tailored cost/latency spreadsheet for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private by 2028-02-07
Priya to propose benchmark spec (QPS, tail latency targets, sample dataset) by 2028-02-06
Schedule 2-hour Dedicated performance run with LucentCommerce infra team week of 2028-02-13
action_items: Jordan Miller: Share Redwood security brief + SOC2 cert link - due 2028-02-05
Priya Desai: Draft benchmark plan and required data format - due 2028-02-06
Maya Lopez: Provide 2 sample production queries and 25k doc subset for eval - due 2028-02-08
Summary: Discovery focused on where to host embeddings/rerank (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and tradeoffs across throughput, embedding dims, hybrid search and vector DB integration. LucentCommerce wants predictable p99 latency for rerank, avoid egress costs, and keep sensitive product catalog in their VPC. Team requested cost model and benchmark spec.
Topics: stack & constraints; current vector DB; target QPS and p99 SLO; embedding dimension options and storage cost; hybrid search (bm25 + dense rerank) vs full fanout; fallback strategies; data residency/SSO/KMS
Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miller (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, jordan from Redwood Inference, and with me is Priya our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex Chen (Head of Search): Good, thanks. we just wrapped a sprint so timing's good.
[00:12] Maya Lopez (ML Eng): Hi, yeah excited — we've been evaluating a couple options for embeddings and rerank.
[00:17] Samir Rao (CTO): quick background - LucentCommerce runs search on top of ES for lexical, we've layered dense vectors with Pinecone for a year, but costs spiked and tail latency is inconsistent.
[00:31] Priya Desai (SE): thanks for the context. can you share the current qps and typical top-k? this helps us size batching and kernel selection.
[00:39] Alex: baseline is about 380 qps peak for product search, 95th is fine, but our biggest worry is p99 during promos when tail rockets to 700-800, rerank is heavy — we do top 100 fanout then rerank top 10 with a cross-encoder.
[01:00] Jordan: ok top 100 fanout is costly. do you always do dense fanout or do you do hybrid — bm25 to narrow then dense?
[01:06] Maya: we do hybrid in most flows - bm25 to 200 then dense top 100 then rerank. but some flows still fanout fully depending on commerce signals.
[01:17] Priya: good, that hybrid pattern maps well to Redwood routing — you can route cheap flows to smaller models or hosted low-cost pool and critical flows to dedicated. curious on your embedding size and current index tech?
[01:28] Alex: embeddings are 1536 dims, generated with an OpenAI-ish model last year. index is Pinecone, but we're hitting vector egress fees and replication overhead when we scale to regions.
[01:40] Samir: and also vendor lock-ish concern, hence exploring self-hosted or dedicated where we can control replication and residency.
[01:47] Jordan: understood. on dimension sizes — 1536 is common, but for rerank you can often get away with 512 or 768 dense vectors combined with rerank model for final scoring. that reduces storage + IO.
[02:01] Maya: we tried 768 in experiments; recall dropped a touch ~0.8% but cost dropped 30%. curious about Redwood's recommended quantization and kernel implications though.
[02:12] Priya: right — Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload. for throughput we favor int8 or 4-bit quant for storage and a dequant path in the kernel. there's small accuracy drift; we surface recommended eval prompts.
[02:27] Alex: how would that integrate with Pinecone? do you keep embeddings external or push to your internal VDB?
[02:33] Priya: options — keep embeddings in customer VDB and call Redwood for rerank/generation only, or host embeddings inside Redwood Dedicated pools and use Redwood's KV/cache layer to reduce vector fetch overhead. each has tradeoffs on egress and latency.
[02:47] Samir: egress is huge for us - cross-region reads from Pinecone killed our margin during last promotion. so private deployment with VPC peering would be ideal, but we need to balance ops burden.
[02:58] Jordan: that's common. Dedicated offers predictable throughput and you can pin regions; Private gives you the most control — on-prem or VPC with KMS. it increases setup time and contract friction though.
[03:12] Alex: timeline wise, we want a pilot within 6 weeks and decision in 10 weeks. success metrics: p99 rerank latency < 120ms, end-to-end query < 220ms for critical flows, and cost per 1M queries under $X (we'll give exact number).
[03:29] Priya: noted. for p99 targets, we'll propose a batching config and latency SLO. also need to know your current cross-encoder runtime; are you using CPU or GPU for rerank?
[03:40] Maya: cross-encoder runs on a single GPU for offline experiments; production currently runs on CPU which is why p99 spikes. thinking of moving rerank to GPU but worried about cost.
[03:50] Priya: Redwood Dedicated can colocate GPU rerank and embedding inference to avoid network hops. plus autoscaling policies can provide burst capacity for promos.
[04:02] Jordan: quick question — are you using KNN in ES or a separate VDB for nearest neighbor?
[04:07] Alex: Pinecone separate. we tried ES-KNN but index rebuild times were horrendous.
[04:12] Priya: ok. for the benchmark we'll test two configurations: 1) keep Pinecone as vector store and call Redwood for rerank (measure egress and latency), 2) move vectors into Redwood Dedicated local stores and measure tail latency and cost savings.
[04:26] Maya: will the Dedicated option reduce egress fees?
[04:29] Jordan: yes, keeping vectors local avoids cloud-to-cloud egress and allows efficient KV cache and prefix caching. also you can use sharded indexes to parallelize fanout.
[04:39] Samir: about sharding — our dataset is 75M product vectors, 1536 dims. what's realistic for shard counts and query fanout?
[04:47] Priya: 75M x 1536 is big. many customers either reduce dims for nearest neighbor or use a two-stage system: smaller dense index for recall + reembed on candidates or use L2 quant/OPQ to compress. sharding often aligned with regions and hot partitions. we'll propose a shard plan in the benchmark doc.
[05:07] Alex: any recommendations on embedding dim? we could retrain to 512 but that is out of cycle for a while.
[05:12] Priya: pragmatic approach — keep your 1536 in cold store and serve 512 distilled embeddings for hot traffic; keep mapping to original ids for rerank if needed. that gives latency wins while preserving quality when you escalate.
[05:27] Maya: that sounds reasonable. curious about hybrid search routing — how can Redwood do bm25 first then dense? do we need to change our query pipeline?
[05:36] Jordan: Redwood's routing layer can accept a bm25 score and a signal to only perform dense lookup on top N. we can also do conditional routing in our SDK so you keep your existing ES pipeline and only invoke the dense path when a certain threshold is met.
[05:50] Samir: security and compliance: we need SSO/SAML, audit logs, and control plane in our VPC. are those available for Dedicated or Private only?
[05:59] Priya: SSO and audit logs supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SSO and tenant-level logs but some enterprises prefer Private for full control over the control plane. we have SOC2 links and KMS integration options — we'll share docs.
[06:14] Alex: what about model variants — smaller embedder for cheap flows and better for conversions? can Redwood do automatic fallback?
[06:21] Jordan: yes, it's policy-driven. you can say route by latency budget or cost budget; Redwood can fall back to a quantized/compact embedder or a cached embedding if available.
[06:31] Maya: caching — how is KV cache managed? we saw mention of prefix/KV caching in your docs but unclear how eviction and write-through works.
[06:40] Priya: our KV cache stores recent vectors/token caches with LRU eviction and can be writable so updates propagate to underlying vector store asynchronously. eviction tunables and TTLs are in the config.
[06:52] Samir: for our pilot we'll need to test cold start behavior too — promos mean new items. how fast can the index absorb new vectors and be queryable?
[07:01] Priya: ingestion latency depends on indexing topology — dedicated local stores can have near-real-time ingest (seconds to low minutes). if you use a remote VDB, indexing speed is bound by that store. we'll document expected times.
[07:15] Alex: on operational burden — if we choose Private (customer-managed control plane) is Redwood doing the orchestration or do we run infra wholly?
[07:24] Jordan: Private gives you the control plane locally; Redwood provides the orchestration package and SRE runbook. you operate nodes with guidance. it's more hands-on vs Dedicated which we run and guarantee SLA.
[07:36] Maya: I want to dig into throughput examples — for 700 qps with 100 fanout what kind of GPU fleet is needed? can you ballpark?
[07:45] Priya: rough ballpark: if you do fanout 100 and rerank cross-encoder on GPU, you'll need multiple GPUs with specialized batching; kernel selection matters — some models do well with continuous batching and KV cache. we'll calculate in the benchmark doc, but expect to reserve Dedicated pods for these peaks or use autoscale bursts.
[08:06] Jordan: also consider offloading rerank to quantized CPU models for non-critical flows; that can shrink GPU hours.
[08:12] Alex: about vector DB compatibility — we don't want a big migration risk. can Redwood talk to Milvus or Weaviate?
[08:19] Priya: we integrate via standard vector store APIs and can support Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone — typically via a connector layer. migration helpers exist and we've done managed syncs for customers.
[08:33] Samir: any notes on replication topology to hit p99 under promos?
[08:37] Priya: replicate hot shards, use multi-region reads, and prefer local replica for latency. failing over to secondary region is built into routing policies.
[08:46] Maya: latency budgets — you mentioned 120ms p99 for rerank. is that realistic with cross-encoder rerank?
[08:53] Priya: for a 10-item cross-encoder on GPU yes; for full top100 cross-encoder on CPU no. many customers do a dense dot-product rerank for first pass then cross-encoder on top10.
[09:06] Alex: we're very concerned about embedding storage costs — what's the per-vector storage delta for 1536 vs 512 vs quantized?
[09:13] Jordan: 1536 float32 is roughly 6KB per vector; 512 float16 ~1KB; int8/4-bit quant reduces further. so large savings at scale. we'll include a detailed cost table.
[09:28] Samir: about pricing model — Hosted per-token/per-embedding, Dedicated is reserved capacity. any blended contracts for pilots?
[09:36] Jordan: pilots often run on Hosted or short-term Dedicated burst credits; we can propose a pilot pricing that blends. will include in follow-up.
[09:44] Alex: what about instrumentation for observability — we need per-route token costs and detailed latency traces to debug p99 spikes.
[09:52] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces and error analysis. we can expose those to your SREs via read-only access.
[10:02] Maya: a few quick clarifying Qs — do you support server-side encryption with customer KMS?
[10:07] Jordan: yes, KMS integration supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports tenant-level encryption and managed KMS.
[10:14] Alex: for the benchmark data set we'll send a 25k product slice with embeddings and queries. Any preferred format?
[10:20] Priya: CSV for metadata + ndjson for documents + parquet for heavy attributes. we'll put exact schema in the benchmark spec.
[10:28] Samir: can we test a fallback policy that reduces dimension on surge? that seems tricky live.
[10:33] Priya: it's policy based — we can precompute compact embeddings and route to them under surge. the complexity is keeping sync and freshness; we'll include sync strategies.
[10:44] Jordan: quick recap then next steps: Jordan sends cost & security docs. Priya sends benchmark spec. Maya provides sample data. schedule Dedicated run week of 2028-02-13. any other asks?
[10:59] Alex: please include estimated time to onboard Private if we wanted to go that route — we need calendar planning.
[11:05] Priya: will include an onboarding timeline for Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
[11:10] Samir: thanks all. sounds good.
[11:13] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[11:18] (meeting ends)
